en: Saṃyutta Nikāya 31.1 (SN 31.1, PTS SN iii 249) 1.
The Chapter on Gandhabbas: The Simple Discourse (Suddhikasutta)
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
… [as before] … The Blessed One said this:

“Bhikkhus, I will teach you about the gods of the gandhabba host. Listen and pay close attention; I will speak. “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you about the gods of the gandhabba host.”
Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, are the devas of the gandhabba host?
There are, bhikkhus, devas who dwell in the fragrance of roots.
“Bhikkhus, there are devas dwelling in the fragrance of heartwood;
there are devas dwelling in the fragrance of softwood;
there are devas dwelling in the fragrance of bark.”
There are, monks, gods dwelling in the fragrance of bark.
There are, monks, gods dwelling in the fragrance of leaves.
There are, monks, gods dwelling in the fragrance of flowers.
There are, monks, deities dwelling in the fragrance of fruits.
There are, monks, deities dwelling in the fragrance of flavors.
There are, monks, deities dwelling in the fragrance of scents.
"These, monks, are called the gods of the Gandhabba host.
Thus was the first [discourse]. *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 31.2 (SN 31.2, PTS SN iii 250).
1. The Chapter on Gandhabbas.
The Discourse on Good Conduct.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the Gandhabba host?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind.”
He has heard:
“The gods of the gandhabba host are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the Gandhabba-kāyika devas!
He, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Gandhabba-kāyika devas.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Gandhabba-kāyika devas.”
The Second.
Saṃyutta Nikāya 31.3 (SN 31.3, PTS SN iii 250) 1.
Gandhabba Vagga (The Chapter on Gandhabbas)
The Discourse on the Giver of Root Fragrance.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:

“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods who dwell in the fragrance of roots? “Bhikkhu, here someone practices good conduct by body, good conduct by speech, and good conduct by mind. He has heard: ‘The gods who dwell in the fragrance of roots have such-and-such a lifespan, such-and-such an experience of pleasure and pain. Having heard this, he thinks: ‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of those very gods! He dwells with a mind that is resolved upon that state. When he dies, he is reborn in the company of those very gods.”
“The deities dwelling in the Root-Fragrance realm are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
“Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the deities dwelling in the Root-Fragrance realm!”
Thus he is a giver of root-fragrances.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of those gods who dwell among the root-fragrances.
This, monk, is the cause... [as before]...
“By what means does someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in the company of the gods dwelling in the fragrance of roots?
This was the third [discourse]. *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 31.4–12 (SN 31.4, PTS SN iii 251).
1. The Chapter on Gandhabbas.
The Group of Nine Discourses on the Givers of Heartwood Fragrance, etc.
Setting at Sāvatthī.
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why here someone, with the breakup of the body, after death,
[is reborn] among the devas dwelling in the fragrance of heartwood … among the devas dwelling in the fragrance of softwood …”
...of the deities dwelling in the scent of bark;
...of the deities dwelling in the scent of inner bark;
...of the deities dwelling in the scent of leaves; ...
...of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of flowers ...
of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of fruits ...
of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of tastes ...
“...is he reborn into the company of the gods who dwell in the fragrance-scented realm?
“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind.
He has heard:”
‘The deities dwelling in the Sāra-fragrance realm are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that upon the breakup of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the deities dwelling in the Sāra-fragrance realm...’
...of the deities dwelling in the scent of heartwood...
of the deities dwelling in the scent of bark...
of the deities dwelling in the scent of inner bark...
...of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of cloth,
...of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of flowers,
...of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of fruit.
‘May I be reborn into the company of those deities who dwell in the fragrance of flavors... or those deities who dwell in the fragrance of scents.
Thus, he becomes a giver of heartwood fragrances... [and so on].
He is a giver of the fragrance of the softwood;
he is a giver of the fragrance of the bark;
he is a giver of the fragrance of the inner bark.
He is a giver of the fragrance of robes;
he is a giver of the fragrance of flowers;
he is a giver of the fragrance of fruits.
He is a giver of flavors and scents...
he is a giver of fragrant scents.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the company of the devas who dwell upon fragrant scents.
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas who dwell in fragrant scents.
The twelfth [sutta].
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 31.13–22 (SN 31.13, PTS SN iii 252)
1. The Chapter on Gandhabbas.
The Ten Discourses on the Benefit of Giving Root-Perfumes.
Setting at Sāvatthī.
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods who dwell in the fragrance of roots?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind.”
He has heard:
"The deities dwelling in the fragrance of roots are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the gods who dwell in the fragrance of roots!
He gives food … [and so on] … he gives drink.
He gives clothing… he gives a vehicle… he gives a garland…
He gives perfume;
he gives ointment;
he gives a bed.
He gives a dwelling place… he gives lighting.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in companionship with the gods who dwell in the fragrance of roots.
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas who dwell in the fragrance of roots.
The Twenty-second [Chapter].
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 31.23–112 (SN 31.23, PTS SN iii 253)
1. The Chapter on Gandhabbas.
The Ninety Discourses on the Benefits of Giving Heartwood Fragrance and Other Gifts.
Setting at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why here some person, with the breakup of the body, after death,
[is reborn] among the gods dwelling in the fragrance of heartwood … among the gods dwelling in the fragrance of softwood …?”
...of the devas dwelling in the scent of bark;
...of the devas dwelling in the scent of inner bark;
...of the devas dwelling in the scent of leaves; ...
...of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of flowers ...
of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of fruits ...
of the deities dwelling in the fragrance of tastes ...
“...is he reborn in the company of the gods who dwell in the fragrance-scented realm?
“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind.
He has heard:”
“The gods who dwell in the realm of fragrant scents are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
“Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of those gods who dwell in the realm of fragrant scents!”
Thus he gives food … [and so on] … he gives drink … he gives clothing …
He gives a vehicle;
he gives a garland;
he gives perfume.
He gives ointment … he gives a bed … he gives a dwelling …
“He gives a lamp.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the devas who dwell in fragrant scents.
This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas who dwell in fragrant scents.”
The one hundred and twelfth.
(Thus, by way of summary, there are one hundred and twelve discourses.
The First Chapter on Gandhabba.
Its summary verse:
The pure good conduct,
and ten others concerning the giver.
The hundredfold benefits of giving are well-expounded regarding the gandhabbas.
The Saṃyutta on the Gandhabba Class is complete.
